_about: The frozen behaviour of the matcher, case by case. Phase 0 of the generic
matching plan: the semantic layer must widen coverage without quietly
losing any of the precision these cases pin down.
Each case is one requirement against one hand-written CV. `expect` names
the relation and evidence location the deterministic matcher must produce
with no LLM involved. `label` is the golden-dataset judgement in the
INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE), which is what precision and recall are computed
against — a case labelled NO_MATCH that produces a relation is a false
`family` groups cases by job family so coverage can be reported per
family rather than as one average that hides a weak one.

Cases carrying `semantic_expected` are the calibration set: they are what `python -m bench.report --calibrate` measures the similarity distribution over. `true` means the FIRST span demonstrates the requirement and retrieval must find it; `false` means no span does and retrieval must offer nothing. Every other case's spans double as negatives for every requirement but their own.

`calibration_group` marks cases that mean the same thing. Their spans are EXCLUDED from each other's negatives during calibration rather than counted as false: "coordinated with physicians and product stakeholders" really does demonstrate cross-functional collaboration, and scoring that pair as a negative would make an accurate model look like it cannot separate the classes.
